title: Native Weil tensor constructions below Verdier duality
statement: Fix a finite field k₀, a prime ℓ invertible in k₀ and a k₀-scheme X. In the actual abelian category of pro-etale Weil module sheaves supplied by [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], define the functorial tensor map in its fixed right argument by conjugating the internal-Hom precomposition transformation under tensorIhomAdjunction. Its identity and composition laws are the conjugation laws. Curried tensor, with its right argument first, is this map together with the existing tensorFunctor; flip it to put the left argument first and totalize cochain complexes by the existing signed direct-sum total tensor of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. NativeIsKFlat requires this actual total tensor to preserve quasi-isomorphisms in each variable. K-flat and K-injective resolution records retain their actual complexes, quasi-isomorphisms and respective properties. For a separated finite-type X, the derived tensor is exactly the tensor of the native closed structure of [lem-sf-weil-native-closed-forgetful], whose internal Hom identifies with the existing derivedHom. On two NativeIsKFlat complexes P,T its object at (QP,QT) is naturally isomorphic to Q of their actual total tensor, naturally in both chain maps. This is precisely the tensor-only part of the previously bundled category-and-operations definition; it introduces no different tensor, resolution notion, or model comparison.

proof.text: Apply the additive-bifunctor K-flat tensor--Hom representability theorem [lem-sf-kflat-bifunctor-tensor-hom] to the actual native tensor/ihom parametrized adjunction. NativeIsKFlat supplies preservation of quasi-isomorphisms in the needed tensor variable, and the native closed comparison supplies the specified product-total Hom representatives.

Compose its natural Hom equivalences with the inverse of the chosen closed adjunction. Representability gives an isomorphism from the chosen derived tensor to the localized total tensor. Evaluate the source-variable naturality identity at the identity map and use target naturality to obtain the required both-variable square.
